stories.title: Suno snatched millions of songs from YouTube, Genius, and Deezer

bullet_points: AI music generator Suno was found to have been trained by scraping millions of songs and lyrics.
The data was sourced from major platforms including YouTube, Deezer, and Genius.
The controversy is amplified by Suno's lack of transparency regarding its training data acquisition.

stories.title: Microsoft’s Secure Boot has been broken for a decade and no one noticed until now
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Microsoft's Secure Boot feature has a long-standing, critical vulnerability.
The vulnerability stems from unrevoked, old 'shims' within the system.
This flaw allows for relatively simple bypasses of the security mechanism.

bullet_points: Murati's Thinking Machines has released a new Large Language Model (LLM).

The LLM boasts a substantial size of 975 billion parameters.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured $88 million in funding from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
The company boasts a significant user base, currently serving 8.9 million developers.
The funding validates the growing importance and adoption of open-source models in the AI ecosystem.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speedup is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% faster improvement according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and lower memory consumption.
The updated engine also enables models to generate higher quality outputs.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
A key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, simplifying the deployment of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing LLM execution on Apple hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Lawsuit claims Meta's layoff decisions were made by AI, not humans
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A lawsuit alleges that Meta utilized Artificial Intelligence in its layoff decisions.
The core of the legal challenge focuses on the potential use of AI in terminating workers with disabilities or medical conditions.
Meta has publicly denied the claim that AI was used to make these specific termination decisions.

stories.title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
stories.author: Wei Zhan
bullet_points: Introduces TerraZero, a new procedural driving simulator and self-play training stack for autonomous vehicles.
Addresses key challenges in AV training: needing high speed, real-world map realism, and diversity for safety-critical scenarios.
Achieves high performance by using a configurable C engine for simulation and GPU for policy inference, sustaining 1.3M agent-steps per second.

stories.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces PalmClaw, a framework designed to enable native, on-device LLM agents for mobile phones.
Addresses the limitation of current agent systems running primarily on powerful desktops/servers, bringing complex task execution to mobile environments.
Highlights the importance of mobile devices as key agent environments due to their accessibility and access to user data and sensors.

stories.title: Audio-Native Speech Recognition with a Frozen Discrete-Diffusion Language Model
stories.author: Vineet Agarwal
bullet_points: Proposes an alternative to traditional autoregressive decoders for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) using a discrete diffusion language model.
The method allows for parallel transcript refinement over a few denoising steps, contrasting with sequential token generation.
Utilizes an audio-native interface trained on DiffusionGemma, a 26B Mixture-of-Experts model, employing a uniform, random-token discrete diffusion process.

stories.title: Resist and Update: Counterfactual Report Coordinates for Incentive-Compatible LLMs
stories.author: Yuen-Hei Yeung
bullet_points: Addresses a critical failure in aligned LLMs: misreporting under non-evidential incentive pressure (e.g., agreeing with a confident user).
Introduces a novel method using 'counterfactual report mediators' to enforce internal incentive-compatibility (IC).
Aims to make LLM outputs robust by ensuring reports are invariant to forbidden influences (like pressure) but responsive to genuine evidence.

stories.title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
stories.author: Wei Zhan
bullet_points: Introduces TerraZero, a new procedural driving simulation and self-play training stack for autonomous vehicles.
Addresses key challenges in autonomous driving training: speed, realism (grounding in map structure), and diversity (covering long-tail safety cases).
Achieves high performance by running simulation on CPU and policy inference on GPU via a zero-copy path, sustaining 1.3M agent-steps per second.

stories.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces PalmClaw, a framework designed for running LLM agents natively on mobile phones.
Addresses the limitation of current agent systems being primarily desktop/server-based, highlighting the importance of mobile environments.
Focuses on enabling mobile agents to perform multi-step tasks and tool-calling directly on user devices.

stories.title: The Illusion of Robustness: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Prediction Flips under Task-Irrelevant Context
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: LLMs appear robust to task-irrelevant context when measured by aggregate accuracy.
This aggregate stability is misleading, as it masks significant per-example prediction instability.
The research highlights a critical vulnerability in how LLMs handle long, context-rich inputs.

stories.title: Stripe, Advent offer to buy PayPal for more than $53B
stories.author: rvz
bullet_points: Major financial technology acquisition news involving PayPal.
Stripe and Advent are the bidders offering to purchase PayPal.
The proposed acquisition value exceeds $53 billion.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It targets complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality directly within Claude Code.
This suggests an enhancement in the capability of local LLM environments to handle complex, real-time tasks.

stories.title: How hard is it to build orbital data centers, actually?
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: The article discusses the engineering challenges of constructing orbital data centers.
A key technical hurdle identified is the expense and weight of current ISS radiators.
The focus of current development efforts is on creating cheaper and lighter thermal management systems for space.

stories.title: US military sent explosive drone boats into combat for the first time
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The US military has deployed explosive drone boats in combat operations.
These drone boats were reportedly used to strike an Iranian naval port.
The deployment signals an escalation in regional military tensions.

stories.title: These painted e-tattoos could be the future of wearable biosensors
stories.author: Jennifer Ouellette
bullet_points: The article discusses the potential of painted e-tattoos as future wearable biosensors.
These sensors utilize conductive ink applied directly onto the skin.
The ink dries to form functional electrodes capable of sensing biological data.

stories.title: Google revamps image search for its 25th anniversary with more images and more AI
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is updating its image search functionality for its 25th anniversary.
The revamped search leverages AI to create personalized, always-updated image galleries.
The personalization is driven by analyzing the user's 'unique interests'.

stories.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
stories.author: Xinyu Feng
bullet_points: Current LLM agents often over-complicate tasks by employing a 'maximum-context-first' strategy, leading to unnecessary overhead.
The research proposes the need for 'task-aware execution-scope estimation' in AI agents.
This capability involves judging a task's true difficulty and determining the most efficient path to completion.

stories.title: FormalAnalyticGeo: A Neural-Symbolic Based Framework for Multimodal Analytic Geometry Problem Generation
stories.author: Qiufeng Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FormalAnalyticGeo, a neural-symbolic framework designed to generate multimodal analytic geometry problems.
Addresses the scarcity of annotated samples in analytic geometry, a domain currently underserved by MLLMs.
Overcomes limitations of existing methods, specifically template methods (inability to handle constraints) and generative models (lack of geometric precision).

stories.title: The Seriality Gap in Video Diffusion Models
stories.author: Yutong Bai
bullet_points: Video diffusion models struggle with predicting long causal chains in complex physical simulations (e.g., multi-ball collisions).
The degradation in performance is linked to the dependent-event structure (interactions) rather than simply the total video length.
Standard bidirectional video diffusion models show reduced accuracy as the sequence of interacting events lengthens.

stories.title: The Spectrum Is Not Enough: When Context Helps Time-Series Forecasting
stories.author: Hasan Kurban
bullet_points: The paper challenges the reliance on spectral indices (like those derived from power spectra) for assessing time-series predictability.
It argues that the true measure of predictability is whether adding contextual information (longer lookback, retrieval, pretraining) improves forecasting, which is a different question.
The value of context is presented as a property of the operating point, not an inherent property of the time series itself.

stories.title: Watermark Forensics for Generative Models: An Information-Theoretic Perspective
stories.author: Jiankun Hu
bullet_points: The research proposes using watermarks in generative model outputs for advanced forensics beyond simple machine detection.
These watermarks can be used to attribute content to a specific user, extract hidden data payloads, or localize surviving content after editing.
The paper analyzes the information-theoretic cost (sample length $n$) required to achieve different levels of forensic capability on this 'forensic ladder'.

stories.title: Robustness of Deep Learning Models for PV Power Forecasting under NWP Forecast Errors: A Spatiotemporal and Physically Interpretable Analysis
stories.author: Xuepeng Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for robust deep learning models in PV power forecasting, moving beyond simple accuracy metrics.
Focuses on the challenge posed by complex, temporally correlated, and physically coupled errors from Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models.
Proposes a spatiotemporal and physically interpretable analysis to evaluate model performance under realistic forecast uncertainties.

stories.title: LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes
stories.author: Henry Moss
bullet_points: Introduces LatentFlow, a general framework designed to condition stochastic processes.
Addresses the difficulty of conditioning stochastic models, which typically requires bespoke, model-specific solutions.
Key feature is that the framework operates without learned neural approximations or training.

stories.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
stories.author: Xinyu Feng
bullet_points: Current LLM agents often lack the ability to estimate the complexity or required effort of a given task.
This leads to inefficient behavior, such as over-auditing simple tasks by re-examining already processed information.
The research proposes developing 'task-aware execution-scope estimation' to guide agents toward the most efficient solution path.

stories.title: MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations
stories.author: Zhiyu Li
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'MemOps' to benchmark memory operations in long-horizon LLM conversations.
Current memory evaluations are criticized for being black-box, only scoring final answer correctness.
MemOps aims to differentiate various memory failures, such as missing facts or using stale data, rather than just final output.

stories.title: LLM Judges Can Be Too Generous When There Is No Reference Answer
stories.author: Sowmya Vajjala
bullet_points: The paper investigates the reliability of using LLMs as judges for evaluating open-ended, no-reference model responses.
It addresses the potential issue of LLM judges being overly generous when no ground-truth answer exists.
The research employs a two-stage pipeline involving calibration and sensitivity experiments to test the judge model's performance.

stories.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Misconceptions in Multi-Turn Medical Conversations
stories.author: Saiph Savage
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for LLMs to handle patient misconceptions in multi-turn medical conversations.
Current evaluation frameworks are insufficient for assessing how LLMs manage evolving or persistent false beliefs in dialogue.
The study focuses on developing methods to ensure safe medical communication by identifying and correcting underlying patient misconceptions.

stories.title: Can LLMs Write Reliable Rubrics? A Meta-Evaluation for Experiment Reproduction
stories.author: Chenghua Lin
bullet_points: The paper addresses the scalability issue of rubric-based evaluation for LLM research agents, especially in paper reproduction tasks.
It introduces the first systematic meta-evaluation of rubrics generated by LLMs for this purpose.
This research aims to reduce the substantial expert effort traditionally required to create paper-specific evaluation rubrics.

stories.title: Knowledgeless Language Models: Suppressing Parametric Recall for Evidence-Grounded Language Modeling
stories.author: Jan Buys
bullet_points: The research addresses the issue of LLMs relying too heavily on internal, potentially outdated 'parametric recall' instead of provided context.
The authors propose 'Knowledge--Less' Language Models (KLLMs) as a new training paradigm to shift LLMs toward evidence-grounded reasoning.
This work investigates modifying the pretraining signal to improve the reliability and contextual grounding of large language models.

stories.title: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Large Language Models: A Survey of Efficient Inference Techniques
stories.author: Jaegul Choo
bullet_points: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) offer theoretical advantages in parallel generation over standard autoregressive models.
Practical speedups in dLLMs require specialized inference mechanisms, such as diffusion-aware caching and reuse.
Recent research is heavily focused on exploring various acceleration techniques across algorithms and architectures to enable practical deployment.

stories.title: The One-Word Census: Answer-Choice Conformity Across 44 Language Models
stories.author: Tapan Parikh
bullet_points: The study investigates answer-choice conformity among 44 different language models when forced to select a single word from many valid options.
A key finding is that the word 'serendipity' was chosen by 41% of the models when prompted to 'pick a word -- any word.'
The research uses a minimal experimental setup (31 single-turn prompts) to characterize this convergence behavior without relying on complex system prompts.

stories.title: Running Gemma 4 26B at 5 tokens/sec on a 13-year-old Xeon with no GPU
stories.author: neomindryan
bullet_points: Demonstrates the feasibility of running large language models (Gemma 4 26B) on legacy CPU hardware.
Achieves a modest inference speed (5 tokens/sec) without specialized GPU acceleration.
Highlights the growing trend of efficient, low-resource AI deployment.

stories.title: Launch HN: Coasty (YC S26) – An API for computer-use agents
stories.author: nkov47
bullet_points: Coasty is an API service designed to power computer-use agents.
Its core function is enabling agents to complete workflows in legacy desktop and web applications lacking usable APIs.
Users provide natural language tasks, select an environment, and supply credentials for the agent to execute the task.

stories.title: The Line Is Not Between Human and Machine... It Is Between Code and Judgment.
stories.author: jugeni
bullet_points: The article discusses the limitations of purely technical fixes (code) in AI/ML pipelines.
The author used a 'hostile model' to critique their own development process, suggesting systemic issues.
It posits that the critical boundary in AI development is not human vs. machine, but rather code vs. judgment.
